purpose: Four-track follow-up: original low-speed calibration; direct CAS/EAS hunt; test-by-test airborne weights and lift data; document and specimen deduplication. Raw historical evidence, not an approved simulator fit.

sources.aircraft: Supermarine Spitfire VA, NACA 1942 Langley specimen (photographed R7347)
sources.report: NACA ACR / Wartime Report L-353, Stalling Characteristics of the Supermarine Spitfire VA Airplane (Vensel and Phillips, September 1942)
sources.location: Printed pp. 2-3 apparatus and figure 5 calibration; printed p. 7 stall IAS and CLmax table; figs 8-19 source time histories
sources.verification: Original PDF table text and page captions reviewed. The report calls speeds indicated; Figure 5 is explicitly the pilot's meter correction, not proof that the separate NACA recorder used that signal.

sources.report: NACA RM L8A06, Flight Measurements of Flying Qualities of a P-47D-30 Airplane (Kraft, Goranson and Reeder, February 1948)
sources.location: PDF pp. 19-20 figure legends and PDF pp. 69-81 figs. 47-59; PDF pp. 2-3 power, CG and loading; figs. 28-32 controlled turns
sources.verification: Original NASA PDF figure legends inspected. Gross weights are per flight-run caption, not proven instantaneous weight at the precise onset of stall; no CAS/EAS inferred.

sources.report: NACA TN 2899, 1953 publication superseding NACA RM L8A06, same tested airframe and experiment
sources.location: Introductory supersession footnote, not a new independent flight experiment
sources.verification: Catalogued as reprint/supersession only; no extra data points counted.

sources.report: NACA MR L5B13B / WR L-717, Flight Measurements of the Flying Qualities of an F6F-3 Airplane III: Stalling Characteristics (Reeder, February 1945)
sources.location: Conclusions and figures 4-13, flight-derived peak normal-force coefficient CN; gross-weight correction for fuel consumed
sources.verification: Original NASA primary report and original text transcription cross-referenced; ranges are published approximate bands, not newly digitized exact points.

sources.report: NACA MR L5B13 / WR L-715, Flight Measurements of the Flying Qualities of an F6F-3 Airplane I: Longitudinal Stability and Control (Reeder, February 1945)
sources.location: Apparatus and definition of service indicated airspeed: swiveling static and shielded total head one chord ahead of left wingtip; nominal standard service meter free from position error
sources.verification: Same BuAer serial and NACA test program as Parts II and III; establishes measurement-chain lead but does not relabel Part III's figures direct CAS.

series.aircraft: Spitfire VA NACA Langley 1942, about 6184 lb
series.source_location: NACA WR L-353, printed p. 7, table Maximum Lift Coefficients for Various Flight Conditions
series.notes: Source column literally says indicated stalling speed; paired CLmax is original report-derived coefficient. Figure 5 corrects a pilot meter and must not automatically be imposed on a different NACA recorded-speed channel. This is Spitfire VA, NOT the modeled full-span BS.543 LF Mk IX.

series.source_location: NACA RM L8A06, PDF pp.19-20 figure legends 47-59; individual plots PDF pp.69-81
series.notes: Weight is reported gross weight of the run in the original figure caption; it must not be overclaimed as an independently measured instantaneous mass at the exact stall moment. Power, canopy and CG vary. These are NOT 14 extracted stall speeds, and wave-off runs 56-57 did NOT reach a complete stall. Figure 58 3000ft, not 5000ft.

series.source_location: NACA WR L-717, original figs.4-13, approximate discussion bands
series.notes: Normal-force coefficient CN is not unconditionally wing aerodynamic CL; original corrected gross weight for fuel used. IAS measurement used dedicated wingtip head (Part I), position-error-free service IAS concept, but no direct numeric CAS/EAS stall speed is transcribed. Powered values include slipstream and must not be transplanted into power-off clean CLmax.

calibration_reviews.axes: pilot's airspeed meter reading (mph) vs correct indicated airspeed (mph); different cruise, glide and landing marks
calibration_reviews.method: NACA recorder calibrated by formation with trailing-head-calibrated comparison aircraft
calibration_reviews.finding: Original chart genuinely includes the low-speed region. It corrects the pilot meter; the table's NACA recording signal is not proven identical to this meter; in addition, corrected indicated does not explicitly establish modern calibrated CAS. Keep original source table IAS. Preliminary figure reading only, NOT released as a numerical correction table.
calibration_reviews.next: Digitize original image to source-point/pixel axis precision; establish whether table IAS is recorder or pilot-meter basis and source-level error definition before CAS*.

calibration_reviews.original_report: NACA WR L-565, Hurricane II Z2963, figure 7
calibration_reviews.finding: Chart relates the separate underwing cockpit pitot/indicator to a trailing-head reference. NACA flight-dynamics time histories used a separate right-wingtip head. Near-stall applicability to recorded stall numbers must be explicitly established before applying correction.
calibration_reviews.next: Resolve the signal path and digitize true measured anchors with documented per-point visual error.

document_lineage.note: 43-6883, instrument-corrected IAS; archival listing and new stall rows point to one Eng-47-1734-A campaign.
43-24777 source family; correction graph cannot be extrapolated down to the 67.5-86 mph stall rows.
One 1942 P-47B specimen and PHQ-M-19-1417-A report; fast-flight PEC not low-speed calibration.
44-1 fuel flight report, not the new NACA P-47D-30 43-3441 experiment.
One Wright Field FS-M-19-1538-A; do not double-score the two transcriptions.
Same airframe; original programme/report references overlap, but confirm exact pages before labeling every trial same experiment.
Minimum-speed records must not be upgraded automatically to 1g power-off stall.
Original ENG-47-1726-A; water-column speed correction is not generic cockpit IAS to CAS.
Comparison text also mentions L1547 and multiple installations; separate individual flights/configurations before weighting.
One 1946 pilot manual; manual table and its PEC are not independent experiment repeats, nor the A&AEE BS.543 measured trials.
Eight indexed configurations and original correction Fig7 are one NACA campaign; distinct from Hurricane I L2026 and Z3564.
Pre-existing Fig5 lead plus ten newly transcribed table conditions refer to the same original trial.
NACA WR L-715 and -717 (Parts I and III) same BuNo 04776; Part I defines instrumentation used by Part III. No independent replication implied.
1953 TN2899 explicitly supersedes 1948 RM L8A06; never use reprint as independent holdout.

R20 42633 and R22 F6F5 58310 are INDEPENDENT airframes, but their 40164 comparison columns can repeat earlier 40164 numbers. Deduplicate only those explicitly identified comparison rows, not entire reports.

source_policy: Zero newly validated direct near-stall CAS or EAS rows in this follow-up; original direct F4U-4 CAS observations and one 1945 Corsair CAS* remain the current supported classifications.

The F6F-3 Part I position-error-free service indicated speed is a major physically stronger anchor but must retain its period label until measured Part III stall speeds, standardized instrument scale and EAS/CAS semantics have been matched.
Do not equate the number of documents, observations, aircraft labels, flight runs, airframes and independent validation groups.
Do not use powered stall CNmax as power-off aerodynamic wing CLmax; nor transfer Spitfire VA data to the BS.543 IX or P-47D-30 to P-47B.
